title: Home LED face mask: Shark CryoGlow (UK retail waiting list)
headline: A new home LED mask is on a UK retailer's waiting list; I found no independent evidence for this device, so this is a market signal, not a finding.
evidenceTier: Retail page text only (brand/retail marketing); no trial or device study found for this model
fit: Unknown. Red-light LED as a category has human data, but I did not search it for this device, and none that I read covered deep skin tones.
displaces: Fits nowhere if a home LED mask is already in use. Replacing one only makes sense with device-specific evidence.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Source: a summary of Boots' page text that mentioned a waiting list for a Shark CryoGlow LED mask. I did not open a product page, so name, price and specifications are unverified.
I did not find device-specific clinical data. Home LED masks vary widely in irradiance and wavelength, so category-level studies do not transfer to a specific model.
What would change the verdict: an independent device test with stated irradiance and dose, including deeper skin tones.

fitAxes.why: Light devices can interact with photosensitising actives; no device-specific guidance found.
Depends on mode (red or blue); not researched.
